original_question: For the class of continuous critical measures that arises when Heine-Stieltjes zeros are modeled as critical configurations rather than global minimizers, can one find a feasible description of the resulting multi-parameter family of continuous critical measures?
target_in_paper: Section 7, item (b), second open problem: for Heine-Stieltjes polynomials whose zeros are critical configurations of the total energy rather than global minimizers, find a feasible description of the resulting multi-parametric family of continuous critical measures.
correct_elements: The draft correctly isolates the paper's second open problem in Section 7(b): it is about continuous critical measures, not equilibrium measures; it is specifically motivated by modeling Heine-Stieltjes zeros as critical configurations rather than global minima of the discrete energy; and it asks for an effective or feasible description of a multi-parameter family, which matches the paper's wording very closely.
missing_details: The paper places the question in the semiclassical or thermodynamic limit n -> infinity, for normalized zero-counting measures of Heine-Stieltjes polynomials.
The discrete objects are zeros of Heine-Stieltjes polynomials that are critical points of the total logarithmic energy E(X), not necessarily global minimizers of E(X).
The measures under discussion are probability measures mu arising as continuous limits of zero-counting measures, not arbitrary continuous measures.

The nearby setup comes from the generalized Lame equation E''(x) + (sum_i gamma_i/(x-a_i)) E'(x) - C(x)/A(x) E(x) = 0 with A(x)=prod_i (x-a_i), whose polynomial solutions are Heine-Stieltjes polynomials.

The classical real-line framework used for the surrounding asymptotic discussion assumes a_0=-1 < a_1 < ... < a_p=1; in the equilibrium case the residues gamma_i are positive and the external field is generated by fixed charges at the a_i.

The paper's immediate characterization of a real-line critical measure is that its logarithmic potential, plus the external field when present, is constant on each connected component of supp(mu), with these constants allowed to differ from one component to another.

The draft does not say that this is the second of two open problems; the first is convergence of discrete critical measures to continuous critical measures and surjectivity onto all such continuous critical measures.

The phrase 'resulting multi-parameter family' should be tied to 'the given class' of continuous critical measures arising in this Heine-Stieltjes semiclassical setting, rather than to an unrestricted family of critical measures.

No ambient-ring, homogeneity, quartic-degree, or nilpotency conditions are relevant in this paper; the omitted structural data are instead the ODE, energy functional, external field, support, and weak-* limit framework.
refined_question: In the semiclassical limit n -> infinity, for Heine-Stieltjes polynomials whose zeros form critical configurations of the discrete logarithmic energy E(X) rather than its global minimum, can one obtain a feasible description of the multi-parameter family of continuous critical probability measures mu on the real line that arise in this Heine-Stieltjes class, where U^mu (together with the external field, when present) is constant on each connected component of supp(mu), with the constants allowed to differ from component to component?
justification: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual wording: the phrase 'find a feasible description of the multi-parametric family of continuous critical measures' is essentially verbatim from Section 7(b), page 12. To make it stand alone and faithful, one has to restore the surrounding context that the paper makes implicit there: this is a semiclassical-limit question for Heine-Stieltjes zero-counting measures; it concerns zeros viewed as critical configurations of the total energy E(X), not global minimizers; and the relevant continuous objects are critical probability measures on the real line, characterized nearby by componentwise constancy of the potential plus external field. Sections 2 and 6 explain why the authors move from global minimizers to critical configurations, while Sections 3 and 7 supply the Heine-Stieltjes/Lame notation and asymptotic setting. The paper does not state an explicit equivalent reformulation of open problem (ii), so none should be added.
